title: Add a full-screen toggle and side-by-side bundle list to the Lore pane mod (opum-doc design of record)
description:
Operator instruction, 2026-10-02, relayed by opum-agent (opum-doc seq 164; opum-agent OPAG-1089): "add full screen mode and a toggle for it for the lore and quest mode." Design of record: opum-doc `docs/reference/pane-full-screen-and-quest-migration-skill-design.md` at main `945d0ae2` (read by ref, 2026-10-02). lore-cli builds exactly the Lore pane half; quest-cli builds the board's toggle and the Backlog.md migration skill.

WHAT THE DESIGN SAYS, section 1, for the Lore pane:
- TOGGLE: hotkey `z` inside the pane, plus a `full` argument to the pane command (`/lore-pane full`). Pressing `z` again, or `full` again, returns to the normal size.
- OPENING FULL: reopen the pane with `focus`, `closeOnEscape` left off, and `columns` = viewport width minus a small transcript margin (~20 columns) when docked, or `rows` = viewport height minus the prompt area when inline. `e.viewport.isFullscreen` says which layout the surface is in. Both are requests, not grants: a size the person dragged or keyed wins, and the surface clamps to what the layout spares.
- REMEMBERED: the full-or-normal choice is stored with the pane's other settings and restored at the next session.
- LAYOUT: in full mode the Lore pane draws the outline or search results beside the document when there are at least 120 body columns, and keeps its normal stacked layout below that.
- HONEST COPY: when the surface keeps a person-dragged size instead, the pane shows the one-line hint "Drag the pane edge to resize; z switches layouts" rather than claiming a size it did not get.
- NOT THIS TASK: the Quest board's `c` collapse rail is a third state on the board, and `c` from full mode collapsing to the rail is quest-cli's half.

TESTS THE DESIGN ASKS FOR: the toggle reopens the pane with the expected `columns`/`rows`; the side-by-side layout draws at 120 or more body columns and the stacked layout below it; the setting survives a reload; each test runs on the terminal AND the desktop surfaces.

GATES: `bun test`, `bun run lore check` run from source as CI does, and the mod gate's own command `node scripts/mod-test.mjs` (the `mod gate (opum-lore plugin)` CI job). The mod harness prints NOT TYPECHECKED on a workstation whose `claude` CLI is newer than the declarations on disk; type by hand against the 2.1.287 declaration and record the declaration's own first line beside the exit code.

PRECEDENT: the pane mod itself is LCLI-664 (squash `dab21352`, landed as opum-ai/lore-cli#466), with its harness at scripts/mod-test.mjs.

IF THE BUILD FORCES THE TRANSCRIPT MARGIN OR ANYTHING ELSE IN THE DESIGN, report it to opum-agent and do not settle it here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `z` inside the pane and the `full` argument to the pane command each toggle between the normal size and the largest size the surface allows, and a second press returns to the normal size.

Docked full mode reopens the pane with `focus` and without `closeOnEscape`, asking for `columns` = the viewport width minus about 20; inline full mode asks for `rows` = the viewport height minus the prompt area. The evidence is the open args the module actually passes, asserted in the mod harness.
The full-or-normal choice is stored with the pane's other settings and restored at the next session.

In full mode at 120 or more body columns the bundle list draws in a left column with the document on the right, on both the Read tab (the browse list, with the open document highlighted) and the Search tab (the results); below that width both tabs keep their stacked layout.
When the surface keeps a person-dragged size instead of the requested one, the pane shows the one-line hint "Drag the pane edge to resize; z switches layouts".
Each of the design's tests -- the toggle's open args, the 120-column layout switch, and the setting surviving a reload -- runs on the terminal and the desktop surface.

`bun test`, `bun run lore check` and the mod gate's own `node scripts/mod-test.mjs` pass on the head, with any workstation-only failure named and its reachability from this diff stated rather than assumed.

implementationNotes: DESIGN CORRECTION, 2026-10-02: the design of record moved to opum-doc main `fea942b` (opum-ai/opum-doc#623). Its first version said the Lore pane draws "the outline or search results beside the document" -- this pane has no outline. This session reported the gap rather than guessing, and opum-doc corrected the wording to mean the bundle list: in full mode at 120 or more body columns a left column holds the bundle list with the document on the right, on both Read (the browse list, with the open document highlighted) and Search (the results); below that width both stay stacked. The correction is recorded in the doc's own Corrections section as a wording fix to an already-requested feature, not a new decision -- proposed DEC-138 was withdrawn. AC position 4 and its test are built to the corrected text.

DESIGN REF MOVED, 2026-10-02: the design is now at opum-doc main `080b63a`. Diffed against `fea942b`, exactly one delta binds this repository -- the inline prompt-area margin is settled at 6 rows (it was unspecified, and this module had chosen 8), applied to PROMPT_AREA_ROWS in the same branch, tests included. The same revision also specifies two things the module already does and now pins with a test: the pane re-asks when the viewport's size changes, and a request within 4 cells of the size drawn counts as granted (the module's SIZE_SLACK). The rest of that diff is quest-cli's rollback wording. The doc's own Corrections section records both as accuracy fixes to an already-requested feature, not new decisions.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, 2026-10-02, routed to opum-doc (opum-agent seq 240) and deliberately NOT settled here -- the operator's rule of 2026-10-02 is that workers decide no design question: the full-size reopen carries `focus: true`, which is what the design says ("Opening full: reopen the pane with `focus`"). The same code path runs on the first draw of a session that remembered full mode, so that session's pane asks for the keyboard before the person has typed anything. The build keeps B (focus as written) on the orchestrator's instruction to hold it until opum-doc answers; if the answer is A -- focus only on a person-initiated toggle, not on a draw that merely applies the remembered mode -- the change is one flag in `requestPane` and the test that asserts it.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW PASS, 2026-10-03, one reviewer over 8702c08f..394b3603 (code-identical to the tip at the time; docs-only commits followed). Findings, each fixed in a following commit:

- F1 CRITICAL, fixed before the pass ended: at `4fe2b05e` the branch still awaited `$.command.register({name:"lore"})` in session.start, which on Claude Code 2.1.288 throws -- `refused: it is the plugin's /opum-lore:lore` -- and skips the WHOLE hook, so the mod was dead: no tool, no pane. `claude plugin validate --strict` and 52 passing mod tests both passed over it. Caught by the live-session gate probe (opum-doc seq 178/180), not by the tests. Fixed by the drop at `394b3603`.
- F2 MEDIUM: the tool's trailing unsized `$.ui.open` reset a requested full size, and when the mode was unchanged nothing re-asked, because the once-only guard still named the old request (reproduced by mounting the pane full BEFORE the call -- the committed tests mounted after, which is why they missed it). Fixed by resetting the guard after that open, with a test that mounts full first.
- F3: stale command references. The reference-doc half was the worker's and is fixed; two comments followed with the code.
- F4: the move had made the Read fallthrough draw the uncommitted-changes strip with no document open, where the base returned early; restored.
- F5: `personRequest` was a one-shot global consumed by whichever draw ran next, not keyed to the request that raised it; keyed.
- F6: a comment claimed the unknown-doc refusal left the view exactly as found; it does not (the read sets isLoading then error). Corrected.
- CARRY-OVER: the deleted command hook refreshed the catalogue on every invocation; the tool now does the same.

VERIFIED CLEAN by the reviewer: the tool's registration (awaited before use) and its exact matcher, argument validation refusing non-string/non-boolean by name, the unknown-id refusal opening nothing else, no `focus` on any tool open, no dangling symbol or stale reference after the drop, and two mutation checks reproducing the predicted red subsets. Also qualified: a "typecheck clean" reading must name the declaration's version, since the mod harness types only against a declaration naming the RUNNING build and otherwise reports NOT TYPECHECKED.
